techniques.name: Basic Step
techniques.tagline: The foundation — 6 steps, two sets of 3
techniques.what: The On2 basic step is the heartbeat of NY-style salsa. You step on counts 1-2-3 and 5-6-7, with a natural pause (break) on counts 4 and 8. That gives you exactly 6 steps per 8-count phrase. Leaders step forward on 1, followers step back on 1. If you find yourself taking more than 6 steps, you are losing the count — reset and simplify.

mechanics.action: Step forward (leader) or back (follower) with your left foot
Step in place or shift weight to right foot
Step back with left foot, returning toward center
BREAK — hold, no step, reset your weight
Step back with right foot (leader) or forward (follower)
Step in place or shift weight to left foot
Step forward with right foot, returning toward center
BREAK — hold, no step, reset your weight

arm_styling.action: Arms relaxed at sides or in partner frame; no exaggerated movement
Mirror the opposite side; keep elbows soft and close to body

instructor_quotes: Count 1-2-3-5-6-7 for a basic step. That's 6 steps total. If you're stepping more, you're losing time and the count.
There's a break between each set of 3 counts: 1-2-3 (break) 5-6-7 (break). Use these breaks to reset and stay on time.
Followers: don't change your basic step when the leader starts going back with their left foot. Keep your normal pattern until the lead signals otherwise.

frames.caption: Opening position — dancers face forward, weight centered, ready to begin basic step on count 1
Mid-basic: dancers have shifted weight and are moving through counts 2-3, bodies angled slightly toward mirror
Basic step traveling — all three dancers moving in unison, demonstrating the 5-6-7 half of the phrase

techniques.drill: Stand alone without music. Say '1-2-3-BREAK-5-6-7-BREAK' out loud while stepping. Do this for 2 full minutes until the pause feels natural. Then add music at half speed.
techniques.common_error: Taking 8 steps instead of 6 — students add an extra step on the break counts (4 and 8). If your feet are always moving, you are never resetting. Force yourself to pause and feel the break.

techniques.name: Prep Step
techniques.tagline: Twist right to unlock the left turn
techniques.what: The prep step is the setup move that signals an upcoming turn. Before a left (inside) turn, you twist your body to the right on counts 1-2. This rightward twist 'loads' your body like a spring — when you release on count 3, you naturally unwind into the left turn. Without the prep, the turn feels forced and off-balance. Think of it as a conversation with your body: twist right first, then the left turn becomes effortless.

mechanics.action: Step forward as in basic, but begin rotating your torso to the right
Complete the rightward body twist — hips and shoulders rotate right, loading the turn
Release the twist; this is where the turn initiates — pivot begins here
Complete the turn and return to basic step position

arm_styling.action: Right arm stays close to body; left arm begins to lift slightly to frame the upcoming turn
Arms frame the turn — right hand guides, left hand lifts

instructor_quotes: Before a left turn, twist your body to the right to prepare. This unlocks you from the right twist into the left twist on count 3.
twist on 2
prep for the turn

frames.caption: Pre-prep: neutral stance before the body twist begins — note the upright posture and centered weight
Body twist visible — torso has rotated, loading the prep before the turn releases on count 3
Prep completing — weight shifting as the body unwinds, about to initiate the turn

techniques.drill: Practice the prep step without turning. Step forward, twist right on 2, then just step back on 3 without turning. Feel the coil and release. Do 8 reps, then add the full turn.
techniques.common_error: Skipping the twist entirely and just stepping forward. Without the rightward body rotation on count 2, the left turn has no momentum and you will feel stuck or have to muscle through it.

techniques.name: Inside Turn (Left Turn)
techniques.tagline: Turn on 3, face forward on 6, style with intention
techniques.what: The inside turn (also called the left turn or traveling left) is the first turn beginners learn in NY On2. The leader signals the turn through the prep step and arm lift; the follower pivots off their right foot on count 3 and completes the rotation to face forward by count 6. The arm styling — keeping your right arm close to your ear and tracing your body from behind your neck down through count 7 — is what separates a clean turn from a sloppy one. Every movement should be deliberate, not tentative.

mechanics.action: Prep step with rightward body twist; arm begins to lift near right ear
TURN HAPPENS HERE — pivot off right foot, left foot swings left, rotation begins
Break — complete the rotation, land facing forward
Right foot steps back (leader) or forward (follower) — you should be facing forward now
Face forward — right leg goes BACK on 6, not forward. Weight stays centered
Step in place — just shift weight, don't move the foot. Stay on time.

arm_styling.action: Keep arm close to your RIGHT EAR — bend it, keep it controlled. Do not let it drift outward
Arm traces behind your neck — intentional, not tentative
Arm traces DOWN the body — from neck to hip, with full intention
Arm traces back UP the body — complete the full trace cycle

instructor_quotes: On count 6, you should be facing forward again after the left turn. Your right leg goes back on 6, not forward—keep your weight centered.
The turn happens on count 3. Your weight shifts and you pivot, but count 7 stays in place—just shift your weight without moving that foot.
Keep your arm styling close to your right ear on counts 1-2-3. Don't let it drift outward; bend it and keep it controlled near your body.
Trace your body with your arm styling from count 5 (behind your neck) through count 7 (down the body) to count 1 (up). Do this with intention, not tentatively.
face forward
keep it close to your ear
trace your body
with intention

frames.caption: Pre-turn: instructor facing forward, arm position neutral — this is the reset before the prep begins
Arm lifting near ear on counts 1-2 — note how the elbow is bent and arm stays close to the head, not drifting out
Count 3 pivot — weight has shifted, rotation is happening, foot is pivoting
Mid-turn: body rotating through the turn, arm controlled near head
Count 6 — dancer should be facing forward here; right leg stepping back, weight centered
Count 7 — weight shift only, foot stays in place; arm beginning to trace down the body
Arm trace in progress — arm moving from behind neck downward along the body with intention

techniques.drill: Do the inside turn without a partner. Count out loud: '1-2-PREP-3-TURN-5-6-FACE FORWARD-7-HOLD.' Freeze on count 6 and check: are you facing the mirror? Is your right foot back? Do this 10 times before adding arm styling.
techniques.common_error: Stepping forward on count 6 instead of back, and letting the arm drift away from the ear during the turn. Both errors throw off your balance and timing. The arm should feel like it's glued near your right ear through counts 1-2-3.

techniques.name: Suzy Q
techniques.tagline: Cross, step, cross — tight, twisted, intentional
techniques.what: The Suzy Q is a solo shine (footwork pattern) done in place. The pattern is cross-step-cross: your back foot crosses behind your front foot, you step to the side, then cross again. The key is keeping your back foot CLOSE behind your front foot — you are not passing your front foot, you are staying tight and controlled. Add hip twist for styling: the visual effect of the Suzy Q comes from the hip rotation, not from how wide your legs go. You can prep the Suzy Q by lifting your right leg on counts 5-6-7-1 before starting the pattern.

mechanics.action: Lift right leg — this is the optional prep before starting the Suzy Q pattern
Cross: back foot crosses CLOSE behind front foot — stay tight, don't pass the front foot
Step: step to the side (small step)
Cross: back foot crosses close behind front foot again
Quarter beat — step only on ODD numbers: count 5
Quarter beat — step only on ODD numbers: count 7. These are the core beats.

arm_styling.action: Arms can mirror the hip twist — opposite arm forward as you cross
Arms settle or prep for next move during quarter beats

instructor_quotes: Cross, step, cross—keep your back foot close behind your front foot. Don't pass your front foot; stay tight and controlled.
When doing Suzy Q, twist your hips for styling. This creates the visual effect of crossing without overextending your legs.
You can prep a Suzy Q by lifting your right leg on counts 5-6-7-1 before starting the cross-step-cross pattern.
After Suzy Q (counts 5-6-7-1-2-3), do quarter beats by stepping only on odd numbers: 1 and 3. These are core beats—just the high numbers.

quarter beats
core beats

frames.caption: Suzy Q cross position — back foot crossing close behind front foot, hips beginning to twist
Suzy Q step — side step between the two crosses, weight transferring
Second cross of Suzy Q — tight footwork, hip twist visible, arms controlled
Quarter beats after Suzy Q — stepping only on odd counts, body settling into rhythm

techniques.drill: Stand still and say 'cross-step-cross' out loud while doing the footwork slowly. Check that your back foot never goes past your front foot. Add hip twist only after the footwork feels automatic. Then add the prep lift on 5-6-7-1.
techniques.common_error: Passing the front foot with the crossing foot, making the pattern too wide. This kills the hip styling and throws off your balance. Keep the cross tight — your feet should almost touch.

techniques.name: Cross Body Lead
techniques.tagline: Guide your follow across your body — assertive, compact, clear
techniques.what: The cross body lead (CBL) is the most fundamental partnered move in NY-style salsa. The leader steps forward on 1, then on count 2 adds a subtle hip twist and arm signal to guide the follower across their body. The follower pivots off their right foot while their left foot swings to the left. Leaders: do NOT step into your follow's space — keep a normal forward step and use body language and touch to communicate direction. Keep your arms at shoulder width around their head — compact, not wide. Followers: keep your right elbow down to maintain frame, and pivot cleanly off your right foot.

mechanics.action: Leader steps forward with left foot — normal step, do not invade follow's space
Leader: subtle hip twist, right hand closer to you, left hand closer to follow — signal the cross
Leader steps to the side, creating the lane for the follower to cross through
Follower pivots off right foot, left foot swings left — crossing through the lane
Follower completes the cross, both dancers reestablish connection
Both return to basic step position, connection restored

arm_styling.action: Leader: twist arm subtly — right hand in, left hand out toward follow. Not exaggerated.
Leader: lift left hand up and out to guide follow through. Keep right hand centered.
Arms at shoulder width around follow's head — compact, controlled, not wide

instructor_quotes: When leading a left turn, twist your arm on count 2 subtly—not exaggerated. Bring your right hand closer to you and your left hand closer to your follow.
Leaders: don't step into your follow's space. Keep a normal step forward but add hip twist on count 2 to signal the left turn.
When leading a left turn, keep your right hand centered and lift your left hand up and out. Don't confuse your follow with mixed signals.
Followers: pivot off your right foot while your left foot swings to the left during a left turn. Keep your right elbow down to maintain frame.
Leaders must be assertive with direction and guide. Use body language and touch to show your follow where to go—don't let them guess.
When turning your follow, keep your arms at shoulder width around their head. Don't use wide arms; stay compact and controlled.
twist on 2
pivot off your right foot

frames.caption: Partner work begins — leader and follower in closed/open position, establishing connection before CBL
Count 1-2: leader stepping forward, beginning the subtle arm twist to signal the cross body lead
Count 3: leader creating the lane, left hand lifting to guide follower through
Follower crossing through — pivoting off right foot, left foot swinging left, right elbow down
CBL completing — both dancers reestablishing connection, returning to basic step position

techniques.drill: Leaders: practice the CBL with a wall. Step forward on 1, twist on 2, step to the side on 3. Feel the lane you create. Then add a partner and focus only on count 2 — make the signal clear but subtle. Followers: practice the pivot alone — stand on your right foot and swing your left foot to the left on count 5.
techniques.common_error: Leaders stepping INTO the follower's space on count 1, blocking the lane they need to cross through. Also: using wide arms instead of compact shoulder-width arms around the follow's head — this confuses the signal and can hit the follower.

choreography.sequence: BASIC STEP -> PREP STEP -> INSIDE TURN (LEFT TURN) -> SUZY Q -> CROSS BODY LEAD (PARTNER WORK)

steps.body: Instructor faces forward toward camera/mirror. Weight centered, feet roughly hip-width apart. Arms relaxed at sides. Two other dancers visible behind — all in starting position.
Dancers have turned to face the mirror (backs to camera). Weight shifting through the basic step. Feet stepping in sequence. Arms relaxed, no styling yet.
Dancers facing mirror, moving through the 5-6-7 half of the basic. Instructor's torso beginning to show slight rightward rotation — the prep is loading. Right leg visible lifting slightly.
Instructor's body has rotated rightward — torso twisted, loading the spring for the left turn. Dancers moving in unison. Weight forward on left foot.
Dancers traveling toward the mirror. Instructor beginning the pivot — weight shifting, foot rotating. The turn is initiating on count 3.
Dancers have completed rotation and are now facing toward the mirror/forward. Right leg stepping back on 6. Weight centered. Arm styling visible — arm tracing near body.
steps.cue: On count 6, you should be facing forward again. Your right leg goes back on 6, not forward

steps.body: Dancers in place — count 7 is a weight shift, not a foot movement. Bodies upright, arms beginning to trace downward along the body.
steps.cue: count 7 stays in place—just shift your weight without moving that foot

steps.body: Dancers performing the Suzy Q footwork. Back foot crossing close behind front foot. Hips twisting for styling. Feet tight — not passing the front foot.
steps.cue: cross, step, cross — keep your back foot close behind your front foot

steps.body: After the cross-step-cross, dancers stepping only on odd counts. Bodies settling. Hips still showing twist from the Suzy Q.
steps.cue: quarter beats — odd numbers only — core beats

steps.body: Suzy Q repeating — dancers showing the cross pattern again. Hip twist more visible. Arms controlled at sides.
Dancers transitioning out of Suzy Q back toward basic step. Weight resetting. Bodies returning to neutral position.
Dancers moving at full music tempo. Instructor facing mirror, stepping through basic. Motion blur visible on feet — speed has increased. Posture upright.
At full speed, the prep step is more compressed. Torso twist happening quickly on count 2. Instructor's body angled right, loading the turn.
Turn happening at full speed. Rotation visible — instructor pivoting. Arm near ear. The turn is compact and controlled even at tempo.
steps.cue: keep it close to your ear

steps.body: Turn completed. Instructor facing forward on 6. Arm tracing down the body on 7. Movement intentional and deliberate even at full speed.
Suzy Q at full tempo. Cross-step-cross happening quickly. Hip twist visible. Feet staying tight — back foot close behind front foot.
Quarter beats after Suzy Q at full speed. Stepping on 5 and 7 only. Bodies bouncing lightly with the music.
Full sequence repeating at tempo. All three dancers in sync. The choreography is flowing — basic into prep into turn into Suzy Q.
Final pass of the solo sequence at full speed. Dancers completing the phrase. Bodies upright, movement controlled.

phases.name: Phase 3: Partner Work — Cross Body Lead

steps.body: Instructor and follower in open position facing each other. Hands connected. Third dancer visible to the right also in partner position. Frame established before the CBL begins.
steps.cue: Leaders must be assertive with direction and guide

steps.move: Cross Body Lead — Leader Steps Forward
steps.body: Leader stepping forward on 1. On count 2, subtle arm twist visible — right hand drawing in, left hand extending toward follower. Hip twist signaling the cross. Leader NOT stepping into follower's space.
steps.cue: twist your arm on count 2 subtly — not exaggerated. Keep a normal step forward but add hip twist on count 2

steps.body: Leader has stepped to the side, creating the lane. Left hand lifting up and out to guide follower through. Right hand centered. Follower beginning to pivot off right foot.
steps.cue: keep your right hand centered and lift your left hand up and out

steps.body: Follower crossing through the lane — pivoting off right foot, left foot swinging left. Right elbow down maintaining frame. Leader's arms compact at shoulder width around follower's head.
steps.cue: pivot off your right foot while your left foot swings to the left. Keep your right elbow down to maintain frame

steps.body: CBL completing. Both dancers reestablishing connection. Follower has crossed through, both returning to basic step position. Arms settling back to open position frame.
steps.cue: When turning your follow, keep your arms at shoulder width around their head. Don't use wide arms; stay compact and controlled

hard_transitions.why: Students often miss the prep entirely because it happens within the basic step — it looks like a basic step but the body twist on count 2 is the signal. If you don't feel the rightward coil loading, you have skipped the prep and the turn will feel forced.

The turn initiates on count 3, which is the THIRD beat of the first set — students often turn too early (on 2) or too late (on 5). The prep twist on 2 must be complete before the pivot begins on 3. Rushing this transition causes the turn to be off-axis.

After the turn, students are often disoriented and lose the count. The Suzy Q starts on count 1 of the next phrase. You must land from the turn, face forward on 6, do the weight-shift-only on 7, and then immediately begin the cross on 1. There is no extra step to recover — you must be ready.

After the quarter beats (stepping only on odd counts 5 and 7), students must return to the full basic step pattern. The rhythm feels different coming out of quarter beats — you are going from sparse stepping back to 6 steps per phrase. Count out loud to stay on time.

drills.name: Solo Basic
drills.instructions: Basic step to slow music. Count 1-2-3-5-6-7 out loud. Focus on 'quick, quick, slow' rhythm.

drills.name: Weight Transfer Check
drills.instructions: Do the basic in front of a mirror. On every step, lift the OTHER foot to confirm full weight transfer.

drills.name: Prep Step Intro
drills.instructions: From basic position, twist your body right on count 2 — this is the prep for the left turn. Just the twist, no turn yet.

sections.name: New Material: Left Turn + Suzy Q

drills.name: Solo Left Turn
drills.instructions: Prep twist right → turn left on count 3 → face forward on count 6. Repeat 16x. Arm stays close to right ear on 1-2-3.

drills.name: Arm Styling Trace
drills.instructions: Do the left turn but focus ONLY on the arm: count 5 behind neck → 7 down body → 1 up. Trace with intention, not tentatively.

drills.name: Suzy Q Footwork
drills.instructions: Cross, step, cross — keep back foot tight behind front foot. Add hip twist for styling. Prep by lifting right leg on 5-6-7-1.

drills.name: Quarter Beats
drills.instructions: After Suzy Q, step only on odd counts: 1 and 3. These are core beats. Count out loud to lock the timing.

drills.name: Walk Through
drills.instructions: Basic → Prep → Left Turn → Suzy Q → Quarter Beats → Basic. No music, just counting. Get the sequence clean.

drills.name: With Music (Slow)
drills.instructions: Same sequence to a slow salsa track. Don't rush the transitions — use the breaks between 3s to reset.

drills.name: With Music (Full Speed)
drills.instructions: Full speed salsa. If you lose the count, stop, find 1, and restart from basic. Don't fake it through.
